title: NEXT F Shared Core Schema Registry
description: Generated index of authoritative Phase 4 Shared Core Schema definitions.

schemas.name: Actor Reference
schemas.description: Compact reference to the actor responsible for an auditable or publishing action.
schemas.purpose: Avoids embedding entire user records in audit, publishing and version contracts.

fields.description: Opaque actor ID when the actor has a persistent identity.
Non-authoritative display snapshot used for human audit readability.
System or integration source identifier for non-human actors.

validationRules.description: Human actor types require actorId.
System/integration actors should identify their source.

delivery.notes: Actor references are internal audit metadata unless another contract explicitly exposes attribution.

schemas.name: Audit Record
schemas.description: Append-only record of a meaningful platform or customer action.
schemas.purpose: Creates one canonical audit envelope for Admin, Customer CMS, integrations and future commerce operations.

fields.description: Minimized before-state data permitted by the affected contract.
Minimized after-state data permitted by the affected contract.

relationships.description: Audit records identify actors through the shared reference.
Audit records target canonical entities when applicable.

validationRules.description: Audit Records are append-only.
before, after, summary and metadata must not contain secrets.
action must use a stable machine identifier defined by the producing domain.

delivery.notes: Audit history is authenticated operational data.

schemas.name: Entity Identity
schemas.description: Stable identity metadata for a canonical NEXT F entity.
schemas.purpose: Provides one reusable identity object so later schemas do not redefine primary IDs and identity creation semantics.

fields.description: Timestamp when the entity was first created.
Timestamp of the latest authoritative mutation.

validationRules.description: id must remain stable for the lifetime of the entity.
updatedAt must not be earlier than createdAt.

delivery.notes: Opaque public entity IDs may be delivered only when the parent contract permits them.

notes: Entity IDs are identifiers, not authorization evidence.
ID prefixes are governed by the Phase 0 naming standard.

schemas.name: Entity Reference
schemas.description: Compact typed reference to another canonical entity.
schemas.purpose: Provides a stable provider-neutral way to reference an entity in logs, versions, events and generic relationships.

validationRules.description: entityType must use a canonical registry machine ID when available.

delivery.notes: May be public only when the referenced entity itself is publicly addressable.

schemas.name: Organization
schemas.description: Minimal canonical tenant organization identity used to scope Sites and platform records.
schemas.purpose: Defines NEXT F business-customer tenancy without treating the customer organization as a commerce buyer or hosting account.

validationRules.description: Organization name must remain non-empty.
Archived Organizations cannot gain new active Site operations without an explicit restoration process.

delivery.notes: Organization tenancy metadata is authenticated platform data. Public business profile content belongs in later content/site settings contracts.

notes: Organization is the canonical NEXT F tenant term. Do not use Client or generic Customer as the machine tenant schema.

schemas.name: Publishing
schemas.description: Reusable publishing lifecycle state for customer-managed content and records.
schemas.purpose: Standardizes draft, review, scheduling, publication and archive state while composing visibility and scheduling.

fields.description: Timestamp when the current published state became effective.
Actor that published the current version.

relationships.description: Publishing attribution uses compact actor references.

validationRules.description: published status requires publishedAt.
scheduled status requires schedule.startsAt.
archived records are not treated as current public content.

delivery.notes: Public payloads may expose selected publication metadata; draft/review operational details should normally remain private.

schemas.name: Revision Pointer
schemas.description: Current/published version pointers for a versioned entity.
schemas.purpose: Allows CMS and API implementations to identify working and published revisions without duplicating version-state fields.

fields.description: Currently published Version Record when one exists.
Whether currentVersionId differs from the active published revision.

relationships.description: Both pointers target canonical Version Records.

validationRules.description: hasUnpublishedChanges must accurately reflect current and published pointers.

delivery.notes: Revision pointers are operational CMS metadata.

schemas.name: Schedule Window
schemas.description: Optional start/end window with explicit timezone semantics.
schemas.purpose: Provides reusable scheduling semantics for publishing and future campaigns without relying on browser-local time.

fields.description: Exclusive or effective end timestamp as defined by the parent contract.
IANA timezone identifier used for human-entered scheduling.

validationRules.description: When both timestamps exist, endsAt must be later than startsAt.
timeZone must be a valid IANA timezone identifier.

delivery.notes: Scheduling metadata is normally operational and omitted from public payloads unless explicitly needed.

schemas.name: Site
schemas.description: Minimal canonical customer website identity and Organization ownership reference.
schemas.purpose: Provides one host-provider-neutral Site record that later manifests, CMS workspaces, content, integrations and health contracts can reference.

fields.description: Current primary public URL reference when configured.
NEXT F platform Site lifecycle status.

relationships.description: Every Site belongs to one Organization.

validationRules.description: organizationId must resolve to the owning Organization.
primaryUrl identifies the website and must not imply NEXT F owns the domain or hosting service.

delivery.notes: Selected Site identity such as name/primaryUrl may be public when a parent API explicitly exposes it. Tenant/control metadata remains private.

notes: Site is hosting-provider neutral. Domain and hosting ownership remain with the customer Organization.

schemas.name: Tenant Scope
schemas.description: Organization and Site ownership context for tenant-scoped entities.
schemas.purpose: Provides a consistent ownership boundary for multi-tenant storage and authorization.

fields.description: Owning Site ID when the entity is Site-scoped.

relationships.description: Tenant isolation follows the constitutional boundary.

validationRules.description: Every tenant-scoped entity requires an Organization.
When siteId is present it must belong to organizationId.

delivery.notes: Tenant scope is internal routing/authorization metadata and is not part of ordinary public content payloads.

notes: Client-supplied organizationId/siteId values must be re-authorized server-side.

schemas.name: Version Record
schemas.description: Immutable historical version snapshot for a versioned entity.
schemas.purpose: Provides one reusable revision format for pages, blog posts, documents, products and other versioned entities.

fields.description: Monotonically increasing version number within the entity.
Immutable canonical entity snapshot for this version.
Optional human-readable reason or change note.
Whether this version was published at least once.

validationRules.description: versionNumber increases monotonically per entity.
snapshot is immutable after Version Record creation.
snapshot must validate against the entity contract/version applicable to the version.

delivery.notes: Version history is operational metadata and must not be publicly exposed by default.

notes: Historical snapshots must not contain secrets excluded by the entity contract.

schemas.name: Visibility
schemas.description: Canonical visibility policy for publishable resources.
schemas.purpose: Separates public discoverability from publishing state so later content types do not invent incompatible visibility labels.

fields.description: Internal explanation for exceptional visibility configuration.

validationRules.description: private and members modes require authentication.
public visibility must not require authentication.

delivery.notes: The visibility object may be exposed selectively, but private/members content itself must not be delivered publicly.

schemas.name: Address
schemas.description: Reusable structured postal or business address.
schemas.purpose: Provides one first-class address object for organizations, commerce customers, locations, billing and shipping contexts.

fields.description: Contact phone associated with this address.

relationships.description: The primitive Address value shape aligns with this first-class reusable schema.

validationRules.description: country must use ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase code.
Postal-code requirements are defined by parent business rules, not globally assumed.

delivery.notes: Public eligibility depends on the parent entity. Private customer billing/shipping addresses remain authenticated data.

schemas.name: Contact Point
schemas.description: Reusable contact method for organizations, locations and customer-facing content.
schemas.purpose: Standardizes phone, email, URL and messaging contact data without hardcoding business-specific fields everywhere.

fields.description: Human-readable label such as Sales or Support.
Canonical contact value validated according to type.
Whether this is the primary contact point within its parent context.
Whether the parent may expose this contact point publicly.

validationRules.description: value must validate according to the declared type.
A parent collection should define at most one primary contact point per applicable contact category unless explicitly allowed.

delivery.notes: Only instances with public=true may be exposed by a public parent payload.

schemas.name: Call to Action
schemas.purpose: Lets pages, services, blog content and commerce surfaces express action intent consistently without defining button presentation.

fields.description: Stable human-readable analytics label when separate from visible text.
Whether the CTA should currently be rendered.

relationships.description: CTA behavior is represented by the canonical Link schema.

validationRules.description: Enabled CTAs require a non-empty label and valid link.

delivery.notes: CTA content is generally eligible for public delivery.

notes: Visual style, radius, color and layout remain frontend concerns unless a later component contract defines controlled variants.

schemas.name: External Reference
schemas.description: Provider-neutral reference from a NEXT F entity to an identifier in an external system.
schemas.purpose: Supports adapters and integrations without changing canonical NEXT F entities to mirror vendor models.

fields.description: Identifier assigned by the external provider.
Optional non-secret provider URL for human navigation.
Timestamp of the last successful synchronization.
Non-secret adapter metadata needed for synchronization.

validationRules.description: provider should resolve to a canonical connector/integration identifier when one exists.
metadata must not contain secrets, refresh tokens or privileged credentials.

delivery.notes: External provider identifiers are technical integration metadata and are private by default.

schemas.name: Link
schemas.description: Canonical destination and behavior metadata for an interactive link.
schemas.purpose: Keeps navigation, CTA, media and content links consistent while leaving visual styling to the frontend.

fields.description: Destination value interpreted according to type.
Request a new browsing context where appropriate.
Accessible label override when visible context is insufficient.
Canonical NEXT F event name emitted for the interaction when configured.

validationRules.description: destination must match the declared link type.
Executable or unsafe URL schemes are prohibited.
External new-tab links should use appropriate rel protection where the renderer does not enforce it automatically.

delivery.notes: Public links are allowed after destination validation.

schemas.name: Media Asset
schemas.description: Provider-neutral metadata for an uploaded or connected media asset.
schemas.purpose: Lets Content, Commerce, Documentation and other modules reference media consistently without coupling contracts to a storage provider.

fields.description: Media duration in seconds when applicable.
Default accessible alternative text for meaningful images.
Public delivery URL only when the asset is intentionally public.

relationships.description: Media ownership follows Site tenant boundaries.

validationRules.description: width/height apply only to media kinds with dimensions.
durationSeconds applies only when the media kind supports duration.
publicUrl must never contain embedded credentials or secrets.
Meaningful public images require appropriate alt text either at asset or reference context.

delivery.notes: Only media explicitly intended for public access may expose publicUrl.

notes: Storage bucket names, private object keys and provider credentials are implementation details and are not required in the public contract.

schemas.name: Media Reference
schemas.description: Contextual reference to a canonical Media Asset.
schemas.purpose: Allows one asset to be reused with context-specific accessibility, caption and role metadata without duplicating the asset.

fields.description: Optional destination when media itself is interactive.

relationships.description: Interactive media may use a shared Link.

validationRules.description: Decorative media should not carry misleading descriptive alt text.
assetId must resolve inside the authorized Site scope.

delivery.notes: Safe contextual media references may appear in public content payloads.
